summary: Not as a dip-buying signal. On BTC, ETH and SOL, going long while %B was below 0, or as it crossed down through 0.05 or back up through 0, did the same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. The result that holds up runs the other way: shorting while %B was above 1 did worse than random on all three timeframes, because price kept rising, mostly in uptrends.

verdicts.use: Buying the dip (%B below 0 or crossing 0.05 and 0)
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. This held for %B below 0, a cross down through 0.05 and a cross back up through 0, in uptrends and downtrends alike.

verdicts.use: Shorting above the upper band (%B above 1)
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 1h, 4h and daily, mostly in uptrends. On 1h and 4h it holds without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles.

verdicts.use: Shorting the cross back down through 1
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 4h, where price kept rising after the cross, but only at 20 and 100 candles. Same as random on 1h and daily.

notes: Going long while %B was below 0 on 1h gave 10,185 entries in 2,542 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.01% ahead of random entries, inside a luck band of -0.13% to 0.14%. The cross back up through 0 fires about half as often and lands in the same place. So does the cross down through 0.05, on 1h, 4h and daily.

On BTC 1h, the cross down through 0.05 beat random by 0.11%, just above a luck band that tops out at 0.10%. It shows at 20 candles only and is the same as random at 10, 50 and 100, so it is fragile. These crosses fire mostly in volatile candles. In a window where price rose overall, the gap reflects price moving more after those candles, not a direction the setting picked.

Shorting while %B was above 1 did 0.25% worse than random after 20 candles on 1h, 0.82% worse on 4h and 5.91% worse after 20 days on daily. On 1h and 4h it shows at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles and holds without its strongest stretch. On daily it shows at 10 and 20 candles only. A close above the upper band marked strength that continued, not a top.

The regimes split this result. In uptrends, shorts above 1 did 0.34% worse than random on 1h and 1.04% worse on 4h. In downtrends the same setting did the same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. Pooled on 4h, the cross down through 1 did 0.49% worse than random, but in uptrends it is fragile and in downtrends it did the same as random.

On daily, the short on a cross down through 1 beat random by 5.16% after 20 days in downtrends, on 65 entries in 45 moves. It holds without its strongest stretch and shows at 50 and 100 days, but not at 10. Pooled across regimes, the same daily short did the same as random. On SOL daily, both shorts look worse than random only because of signals between Jan 3, 2021 and Feb 24, 2021 for above 1, and between Jan 5, 2021 and Feb 25, 2021 for the cross down through 1.

For a long DCA bot, a %B dip condition adds nothing on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work. %B carries information above 1. A short bot that opens on closes above the upper band trades against continuation, most of all while the pair is above its 200-day SMA. If you run shorts, you can leave %B above 1 out of the start condition. Or you can use the daily cross down through 1 only beside a downtrend filter, the one regime where it beat random.
